name: Hall in Tirol Altstadt
kurzbeschreibung: The historic Altstadt of Hall in Tirol enchants as western Austria's largest old town, featuring Late Gothic alleys, Burg Hasegg, and the Münzerturm.
preis: Altstadt kostenlos; Museum & Turm Erwachsene 13,00 €, Kinder 9,00 €
oeffnungszeiten: Altstadt ganzjährig frei zugänglich; Museum Burg Hasegg Di–So 10:00–17:00 Uhr
beschreibung:
Overview

The Altstadt von Hall in Tirol – situated in the Tyrolean Inntal valley around ten kilometres east of the provincial capital Innsbruck – is the largest and most completely preserved historic old town ensemble in western Austria in terms of area. Shaped by more than 700 years of tradition as a flourishing salt-production, shipping, and minting hub, the car-free town centre resembles a magnificent open-air museum of Late Gothic architecture. Harmoniously curved lanes, stately town houses with polygonal bay windows and battlements, as well as historic squares lend Hall an incomparable medieval flair.

History & Architecture

Hall's economic rise was rooted in 'white gold': salt mining in the Halltal valley started as early as the 13th century; in 1303, Duke Otto of Carinthia granted town privileges to the salt settlement. In the late Middle Ages, Hall evolved into the central goods transshipment port along the River Inn. A worldwide historical turning point arrived in 1477: sovereign prince Erzherzog Sigmund der Münzreiche transferred the sovereign mint from Meran to Hall. Here, in 1486, he ordered the minting of the Guldiner, the world's first full-value large silver coin – the historical archetype of the thaler and namesake of today's dollar. From 1567, the fortified Burg Hasegg functioned as the imperial mint, where revolutionary roller coin minting was invented. The town's architectural landmark is the dodecagonal, 46-metre-high Münzerturm of Burg Hasegg. Other highlights of the historic ensemble include the Obere Stadtplatz with the Gothic Town Hall (1447), the three-aisled parish church of St. Nikolaus with its magnificent ceiling frescoes, and the historic Stiftsplatz. Hall was honored with the prestigious Austrian State Prize for Monument Protection for its exemplary historic town revitalisation.

Visit & Getting There

The pedestrian zone of the old town of Hall is freely accessible free of charge year-round around the clock. The Münze Hall museum and the Münzerturm in Burg Hasegg are open from April to October from Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (in winter Tue–Sat 10:00–17:00, closed on Mondays). Admission for museum & tower (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults €13.00, seniors/students €11.00, children (6–16 years) €9.00, family ticket €28.00; admission is free with the Innsbruck Card. Guided town walks depart several times a week from the tourist office on Unterer Stadtplatz. Public transport arrival: S-Bahn Tirol (lines S4, S5) from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof to Hall in Tirol station (approx. 9 minutes travel time), followed by about a 7-minute walk to the centre; alternatively, bus routes 504 and 505 travel directly to Unterer Stadtplatz. By car: Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Hall Mitte), underground car parks Altstadt or Unterer Stadtplatz.

Tips

The historic cobblestones of the traffic-calmed old town are largely level and well navigable with strollers and wheelchairs; access to the Münze Hall museum on the ground floor is wheelchair-accessible (the tower ascent features 204 historic steps). Enjoy the Italian atmosphere at the sidewalk cafés on Obere Stadtplatz and browse the traditional Hall farmers' market, held every Saturday morning.
